theorem_title: A finite monotone palette cannot decrease along too long a rising path
natural_language_statement:
Let $r,B\in\mathbb N$, let $f_0,\ldots,f_{r-1}:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be nondecreasing on inputs at least $B$, and let $\sigma:\mathbb N\to\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$. Let $V:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfy $V(n)=f_{\sigma(n)}(n)$ for $n\ge B$.

Let $x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ have $x_0\ge B$ and $x_k\le x_{k+1}$ for $k<r$. Then it is impossible that

$$
\forall k<r,\quad V(x_{k+1})<V(x_k).
$$

This is a finite pigeonhole obstruction for ranks selected from monotone functions; it is independent of Collatz.
formal_statement:
theorem CollatzWork.finitePalette_path_obstruction
    (r B : Nat) (V : Nat → Nat) (f : Fin r → Nat → Nat)
    (selector : Nat → Fin r) (x : Nat → Nat)
    (hf : ∀ i a b, B ≤ a → a ≤ b → f i a ≤ f i b)
    (hV : ∀ n, B ≤ n → V n = f (selector n) n)
    (hB : B ≤ x 0)
    (hx : ∀ k, k < r → x k ≤ x (k + 1))
    (hdec : ∀ k, k < r → V (x (k + 1)) < V (x k)) : False := by sorry
